_comment: CLIP — a short RECORDING per run instead of a still, answered Yes / No / Other.

Use it for something that only exists while it moves: an animation, a transition, a bug you cannot photograph. For anything he should DRIVE — drag, hover, resize — use live.json instead; four clip steps were rejected in 2026-08-31 as 'just rough to compare'.
Make the recordings first: scripts/ui-review/record-pair.sh <scene> <before run> <after run> <images folder>/clips. build refuses a step whose files are not on disk.
title: The session strip — how it moves, before and after
_comment_title: title: what this deck is about, in his words.
_comment_key: key: a short name for this deck. His answers are saved under it.
_comment_out: out: the page build writes, beside this spec.
_comment_images: images: the folder holding the pictures AND the clips/ folder under it. It must contain this file's own name.

runs._comment: runs: two recordings of the same scene — one off master, one off your branch. One run named "today" is fine when there is nothing to compare against.

_comment_themes: themes: a recording is filmed in ONE palette, so list the one it was filmed in.

steps._comment: One step is one motion. Say in words what to watch for — a recording plays once and he may miss it.
steps._comment_id: id: your name for this point. It labels his answer.
steps._comment_surface: surface: the part of the app this lives in, named the way he would name it.
steps.path: The row of sessions along the top
steps._comment_path: path: how he would get there.
steps._comment_clip: clip: the scene NAME, when record-pair.sh made the files — it looks for <images>/clips/<name>--before.webm and <name>--after.webm, plus a .webp poster beside each.
steps.headline: Switching sessions now slides the conversation in instead of blinking it in.
steps._comment_headline: headline: the one sentence he reads first. What he SEES. 25 words at most, no code words.
steps.changed: The conversation moves in from the right while it fades, over about a third of a second.
steps._comment_changed: changed: the What changed card. One or two sentences on the real difference.
steps._comment_measured: measured: the timing. On a motion step this is the most useful number you have.
steps.notice: Switching feels like moving between two things rather than the screen being replaced.
steps._comment_notice: notice: the You'll notice card. What is different for him while using it.
steps.risk: A long conversation costs no more than a short one, because only the whole view moves.

steps._comment: The same step with the files named by hand — for clips you did not make with record-pair.sh.
steps.path: The row of sessions along the top

clip._comment: clip as an object: one file per run, relative to this spec. Every run in "runs" needs an entry.

steps.headline: Dragging a session sideways now pushes its neighbours out of the way as you go.
steps.changed: The other sessions step aside while you drag, instead of jumping into place when you let go.
steps.notice: You can see where the session will land before you drop it.
steps.risk: Dragging fast over several neighbours puts a lot of motion on screen at once.
